item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00296","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C16","C10","C22"],"selected_candidate_label":"C16","confidence":0.82,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C16 plausibly supplied a material template for the child. Both are personal letters thanking a departing public servant, opening with appreciation for service, acknowledging the burden or disruption caused by the assignment, crediting the recipient's distinctive qualifications and accomplishments, and closing by anticipating continued service in an advisory or consultative role. C22 is a more general appreciation letter and is substantially weaker.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I want to express my appreciation of your service as United States Representative on the Commission on the Status of Women","parent_excerpt":"I want you to know how much I appreciate all that you have done","explanation":"Both open by directly expressing appreciation for the recipient's completed public assignment."},{"child_excerpt":"I am well aware that you have carried the work of this Commission at a great sacrifice to your heavy law practice.","parent_excerpt":"I know how greatly this assignment disrupted your plans","explanation":"Both specifically acknowledge the personal or professional burden imposed by the temporary public service."},{"child_excerpt":"I hope that even though your term of office has expired, we may call on you from time to time for consultation","parent_excerpt":"all that you will do in the future as a consultant and adviser","explanation":"Both close the service-recognition letter by retaining the departing official for future consultation or advice."},{"child_excerpt":"The Commission has benefited by your practical experience as a member of the Bar","parent_excerpt":"The Chiefs have made outstanding progress since you became their presiding officer","explanation":"Each attributes the organization's progress to the recipient's distinctive contribution during the assignment."}]}
